subject.title: Synchronous crypto.createHash blocks Node.js event loop on large MCP schemas

question: Should this issue be treated as enough proof to queue a bundle-MCP config-hash performance fix, or should maintainers first require a focused reproduction that distinguishes large launch config from large returned tool schemas?
rationale: Source proves synchronous hashing exists, but the reported schema example appears to target a separate returned-tool catalog path, and the correct fix boundary changes depending on which payload blocks the Gateway.

options.title: Ask For Focused Reproduction
options.body: Request a small repro or benchmark that shows whether large `mcp.servers` launch config or returned tool schemas cause current-main heartbeat delay before queueing automation.

options.title: Queue Config-Hash Repair
options.body: Treat the synchronous config-hash source evidence as sufficient and ask for a bounded repair in the CLI bundle-MCP preparation path with regression coverage.

options.title: Split Schema Catalog Follow-Up
options.body: Keep this issue scoped to config hashing and open or use a separate item if a returned-schema catalog repro is provided.

recommendation.title: Ask For Focused Reproduction
recommendation.body: Request a small repro or benchmark that shows whether large `mcp.servers` launch config or returned tool schemas cause current-main heartbeat delay before queueing automation.

likelyOwner.reason: The current shipped bundle-MCP config module and adjacent extraction history point closest to vincentkoc for deciding the config-hash boundary.
